text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Monarchist Party elected Guri Durollari as its new chairman at a congress boycotted by 15 of the party's 37 local branches.

- The pretender to the Albanian throne, Leka the First, told the Monarchist Party's congress the present government lacked a legal and historical basis, repeating his call for a referendum on the country's constitutional future.

- The paper alleges the results of a poll conducted for the European Union's Eurobarometer, to be published next year, were manipulated because the organisation that conducted the poll was headed by the wife of deputy foreign minister Arjan Starova.

- The paper says there was a danger of a police state being installed in Albania after police, which has not allowed lawyers to meet suspects charged with charges of trafficking in weapons and women, has now decided to bar prosecutors from interrogating such suspects.

- Lawyers for Klement Kolaneci, the son-in-law of Albania's late dictator Enver Hoxha, have presented new evidence to court in a bid to get him released from jail where he is held on charges of heading a terrorist band.
- Two new suspected money schemes set up office in the southern town of Gjirokaster.
- Albania's A.S.A. group to build a $3.8 million service centre for Mercedes Benz cars near the capital Tirana.

- The ruling Democratic Party has suspended Azem Hajdari from its National Council, the party's executive body, alleging he intervened in the internal affairs of the Independent Trade Union council, called for strikes and attacked the Democratic Party government.

- Albania has been suspended indefinitely by the FIFA, world soccer's governing body. The fate of a World Cup qualifier group nine match between Albania and Ireland in Belfast scheduled for December 14 remains uncertain.
- More than 1,000 Roman Catholic, Moslem and Orthodox believers staged a peaceful march in the northern town of Shkoder to appeal against abortion and killings.
